newsitem.title: POLAND: Gdansk shipyard, Solidarity birthplace, sacks staff.
newsitem.headline: Gdansk shipyard, Solidarity birthplace, sacks staff.

text.p: Shocked workers at the shipyard which gave birth to the Solidarity trade union learnt on Thursday that efforts to save the bankrupt enterprise had failed and they would all lose their jobs.

"I have to dismiss everyone. From today we are beginning the process of sacking 3,800 shipyard workers," receiver Wieslaw Szaj told Reuters after delivering the same grim message to employees at the yard where Lech Walesa founded Solidarity 17 years ago.
The coup de grace fell on Wednesday when the Polish Pekao SA bank refused a $100 million loan for construction of five ships for a German shipowner, saying the contract terms were unsatisfactory.
The receiver had hoped that a loan and the German contract would keep part of the yard alive while he and the government sought an investor to save the business.

Pekao left open a slim possibility of a loan if the German deal was renegotiated, but last hopes faded when the yard's debts reached 415 million zlotys ($136 million) and banks refused further credit. The shipyard had operated under bankruptcy rules since last August.

"Let's not enter any more talks about saving the shipyard because it's just a waste of time," the yard's Solidarity union chief Jerzy Borowczak told about 1,200 stunned and angry workers, adding that they had all been deceived.
The government, dominated by ex-communists, blames the yard's misfortune on its previous Solidarity-backed management and has refused to bail it out.

But Solidarity, which toppled communism in Poland in 1989, says the government has subsidised other loss-making state-owned enterprises and is denying help because of the yard's opposition links and historical role.

Solidarity has grouped rightist opposition parties in a powerful alliance which is leading opinion polls and could beat the current leftist coalition in parliamentary elections due around September this year.
Even if the Solidarity alliance wins, it will probably be too late for the Gdansk shipyard.

The unionists say they feel betrayed, charging that the cabinet had promised the shipyard's bankruptcy was just a legal procedure for its overhaul and had then kept hopes of a recovery alive with prospects of credit.
"It has been a perfidious way of killing us slowly, in instalments," the deputy head of shipyard's Solidarity, Roman Galezewski, told reporters on Wednesday. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
